sentences.text: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
Applicant is in judicial custody in FIR No. 73 of 2022, under Section 376-D, 506 IPC, Police Station Banbasa (now investigated by P.S. Khatima), District Udham Singh Nagar.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.

According to the FIR, on 17.08.2022 at 4:00 PM, when the informant had finished her work in the factory, the applicant took her alongwith him and some other friends and raped her collectively in the forest.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the statements of the victim is not reliable.

In the FIR, she has alleged against three persons and has stated that she was taken in the car, but in her statement under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ("the Code") she has stated that the applicant and the co-accused had come on two motorcycles and in court again, she has introduced car as well as motorcycle both.
The victim before the Investigating Officer, has named one person Farid also, as the person, who raped her.
It is argued that as to how could the victim tell about Farid?
It is not clear.

Learned counsel would also submit that in the examination in the court,
the victim has also stated that she was given cold drink, due to which, she became unconscious and in that state, she was raped.
Subsequently, when she got consciousness, an old woman was giving her water.
Then she called her husband.
5. Learned State counsel would admit that there is discrepancy in her statements.

sentences.text: It is a stage of bail.
Much of the discussion is not expected of.
Arguments are being appreciated with the caveat that any observation made in this order shall have no bearing at any subsequent stage of the trial or in any other proceedings.
7. Initially, in the FIR, allegations were levelled against three persons, two were named and they allegedly took the in a car.
During investigation, the victim has stated that the applicant and co-accused had come on two motorcycles.
In her statement under Section 164 of the Code, the victim has named Rajveer and has not named any other co-accused, whom she has named in statements under Section 161 of the Code.

In the courts, the victim has introduced the car as well as the motorcycle both and has stated that she was given some drinks, due to which she lost her consciousness and in that state, she was raped.
8. Having considered the nature of statements of the victim and other attending factors, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
(Ravindra Maithani, J) 11.06.2024 Jitendra Dalchand Kashyap @ Rajveer @ Rajeev vs State Of Uttarakhand on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186490913/
